newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end higher in erratic trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end higher in erratic trade.

text.p: Share prices finished modestly higher on Wednesday at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) in lighter activity after two days of hectic trade, brokers said.
"It was a comparatively dull day after two exciting days," said Arun Chitkara at broking firm Jamnadas Morarji & Co.
The market plunged in the past two days before a late recovery pulled it up at close on Tuesday.
"The market had over-reacted," he said. "The 3,000 level is a major support level."
The 30-share BSE index closed 9.52 points, or 0.31 percent, higher at a provisional 3,036.87.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index ended 0.19 points, or 0.02 percent, up at 874.19 and the 500-share CRISIL index gained 2.6 points to 586.44, both provisional closings.
An eagerly awaited court ruling on giving protection to former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao against arrest in a forgery case did not have impact on the market.
A Delhi court extended the protection, against unbailable arrest warrant issued by a lower court on Friday, until October 14 when formal charges are expected to be filed against Rao.
"You can expect a one-shot reaction when it happens," one trader said. "Not now, it's partly discounted."
Traders said state-run insurance firms were buyers for the second straight day, but there was little other support.
Software stock Infosys Technologies rose 18 rupees to 649 ahead of first half results.
After trading ended, the firm said its net profit jumped 76.15 percent to 141.1 million rupees in the six months to September 30, 1996, from 80.1 million in year-ago period.
It set interim dividend of 1.5 rupees per 10-rupee face value stock.
SBI rose 3.25 rupees to 212.50, M&M 6.75 to 312.25, Grasim 8.75 to 390, Bajaj Auto 2.25 to 875.75 and Glaxo 7.0 to 203.
